When Disney was… Disney!

One Hundred One Dalmatians (1961) features an iconic scene where Pongo arranges a romantic “meet-cute” between his owner, Roger, and Anita. This was one of the first times Disney used dogs as the main matchmakers in a story, giving the animals more control and planning ability than the human characters.

The film was also groundbreaking for technical reasons. It was the first Disney animated feature to use the Xerography process, a type of photocopying technology. This method was needed to draw more than six million spots for the 101 puppies. It also created the rougher, sketch-like lines seen in the film, which gave it its unique mid-century modern style.
